fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is tensile characterization rather than the HEBM-plus-SPS processing comparison central to the target.
It omits the nanocrystalline FCC/BCC structural state, densification, and milling-induced lattice strain and dislocation accumulation.
The asserted link between high configurational entropy, low lattice friction, and high grain-boundary mobility is unsupported and is not generally implied by the high-entropy concept.
The predicted low strength and high ductility do not reconstruct the reported hardness and compressive-strength enhancement or limited ductility/intergranular fracture.
The falsification rule is non-quantitative and does not independently distinguish dislocation glide from grain-boundary sliding.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses deformation of nominally equimolar CoCrFeNiTi and proposes potentially useful in-situ measurements, so it has limited problem alignment. However, it misses the decisive controlled comparison: varying high-energy ball milling and SPS conditions against the porous, heterogeneous starting or cast state. It also misses the reported mediator—sub-48 nm grains, high defect density, reduced porosity, and an approximately 83% FCC/17% BCC structure—and the associated Hall–Petch, dislocation, and solid-solution strengthening mechanism. No evidence supports the claimed entropy-driven grain-boundary mobility, and neither grain-boundary sliding nor lattice friction is directly measured. A valid falsification test would require quantitative phase/grain-size/defect measurements and controls that vary milling duration or sintering temperature while testing whether strength tracks those mediators.
